items.followUp: State the two conditions required for rotational and translational equilibrium.

rubric.why: A body is in translational equilibrium when the resultant force on it is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant (net) force is zero.

rubric.why: A body is in rotational equilibrium when the resultant torque (moment) on it is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque (moment) is zero.

modelAnswer: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero (translational equilibrium).
The resultant torque acting on a body must be zero (rotational equilibrium).

items.followUp: A 2 kg object moves at 10 m s⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to SI units and the kinetic-energy formula identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating m = 0.5 kg, v = 15 m s⁻¹, and K.E. = ½mv².

rubric.why: This is the correctly calculated kinetic energy with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution and final answer of 56.25 J.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, v = 15 m s⁻¹
Substitution: K.E. = ½ × 0.5 kg × (15 m s⁻¹)²

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive the relation K.E. = ½mv² for a body starting from rest.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is defined as the energy a body possesses because of its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining kinetic energy as the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

rubric.why: Work done on the body is expressed using force and displacement, with force related to mass and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using W = Fs and F = ma.

rubric.why: The equation of motion gives the displacement, with the initial velocity zero for a body starting from rest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using v² = u² + 2as (or its rearrangement) and u = 0.

rubric.why: Substitution into the work expression gives the required kinetic-energy relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving or stating K.E. = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Work done, W = Fs, and F = ma.
For a body starting from rest, u = 0 and v² = u² + 2as, so s = v²/(2a).

items.followUp: Write 72,000 in scientific notation and state the rule for the coefficient.

rubric.why: Scientific notation writes a number as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten, with the coefficient from 1 up to but not including 10.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the form a × 10ⁿ and the coefficient rule 1 ≤ a < 10.

rubric.why: This is a correctly expressed example of scientific notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as 45000 = 4.5 × 10⁴.

modelAnswer: Scientific notation expresses a number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.
